full_judgment:
4. On the other hand respondent's case, in brief, is that Hazrat Rupchan Shah (R) established the mosque in the year 1885 on a land measuring 12 decimals. After the death of Hazrat Rupchan Shah (R), his heirs Bakor Ali, Kosom Ali maintained the property. After the death of Bakor Ali, Kosom Ali, Niamath Ali, Serjart Ali maintained the property and CS Khatian No. 39 was prepared in their names. When Kosom Ali died, Gulam Ali, Basarath Ali, Abdul Hakim, Mowlana Rahmath All and others took the charge of maintenance of the property and RS Khatian No. 209 was prepared in their names. Mow lava Abu Baker Siddique Faraqui being heirs of Mowlana Rahrnath Ali enrolled the waqf property with Waqf Administrator vide EC No. 16832 on 25-11-1991. The waqf property was enrolled in the name of Hazrat Rupchan Saha (R) mosque waqf estate. 

 5. at the time of enrollment 24 decimals was shown to have been taken on lease from the Government vide lease deed No. 1692 dated 15-3-1990. Akkona Begum and Joynab Khatun also gifted ½ decimals land in favour of Waqf estate. 12 decimals land in plot No. 12163 appertaining to khatian No. 209 and 24 decimals of land in plot No. 13554 appertaining to khatian No. 149 along with the ½ decimals land gifted in favour of the waqf estate (total (12 + 24 + ½ ) = 36½ decimals land) was enlisted in the name of the waqf estate. 

 6. After the enrollment of the waqf estate in the name of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque Waqf Estate, Md Tofazel Hossain predecessor of the appellant filed an application on 12-12-1999 for enrollment of waqf estate in respect of 19 decimals of land in plot No.12163 and 12166 appertaining to khatian No. 209 in the name of Kagatia Eshatul Madrassa Waqf Estate. Md Tofazel Hossain also filed another application on 14-5-2000. On receipt of the application the waqf Administrator initiated EC Case No. 1 of 2000 and asked the Waqf Inspector to hold an inquiry. Waqf Inspector after inquiry submitted a report on 12-1-2000. In the report dated 12-1-2000 the Waqf Inspector made a recommendation for enrollment of 19 decimals of land in the name of Kagatia Eshatul Ulum Madrassa Waqf Estate and also recommended for appointment of Mr Md Tafazzal Hossain as Mutuwalli of the waqf estate. 

 7. The respondent filed an objection against the said inquiry report. The Waqf Administrator after receiving the inquiry report heard both the parties and by his order dated 30-9-2002 changed the name of Waqf Estate by replacing Kakadia Eshatul Ulum Madrasha Waqf Estate in place of Hazrat Rupchand Shah Fakir (R) Mosque Waqf Estate and appointed Md Tofazzal Hossain as Mu tawalli/Secretary of the waqf estate and also gave approval of a committee and further gave a supplementary enrollment including 7.5 decimal land in favour of the waqf estate. Thus enrollment was given in respect of 43.5 decimals of land. 

 14. He next submits that the appellant's claim is supported by the deed dated 16-5-1940 whereas the respondent has failed to show any document with regard to 19 decimals of land and on their mere assertion it is not proper to enroll the property as Waqf property in the name of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque Waqf Estate and in that view of the matter the Waqf Administrator rightly passed the order. In the facts and circumstances, interference with the order of the Waqf Administrator by the Additional District Judge is improper, unjust and liable to be set-aside. Mr Abdul Alien Miah Jewel in support of his contention refers to the case of Mohiuddin Howlader vs Abur Rashid & others, 35 DLR (AD) 36. 

 15. On the other hand Mr Lokman Karim, learned advocate appearing for the respondent in his submission appraises the back ground of establishment of Hazrat Rupchan shah (R) Fakir Masjid Waqf Estate and its enrollment in EC No. 16832 on 25-11-1991. 

 17. He further submits that the waqf Administrator has virtually replaced Kagatia Eshatul Ulum Madrassa Waqf Estate in place of Hazrat Rpuchan Shah (R) Masjid Waqf Estate without taking notice of filing of Title Suit No. 150 of 2001, where the alleged deed dated 16-5-1940 was under challenged. As the order passed by the Waqf Administrator is illegal, learned Additional District Judge rightly passed the judgment and order. 

 19. He also submits that the Waqf Administrator treating the application filed by the M.Toffazzol Hossain under section 47 of the Waqf Ordinance passed the order. He could at best have treated the same as an application under Section 50 of the Ordinance and without treating the application under Section 50 of the Ordinance, he wrongly and erroneously passed the order. Therefore, the learned Additional District Judge rightly interfered with the order. In support of his submission he refers to the cases of Md Abdul Mannan vs the Administrators of Waqf 5 CLR (2017) (H D) 390, Bashiruddin Ahmed vs A. Rah an 1986 BLD (HCD) 128. Mr Lokman Karim also subunits that the wag' administrator wrongly included the lease out property in favour of the Kagadia Eshtul Ulum Madrassa. Though it is admitted fact that the 24 decimals land was leased out in favour of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Masjid Waqf Estate. 

 20. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the record and other relevant materials. In this particular case dispute arose between the parties when Kagadia Eshatul Ulam Madrassa Waqf Estate was given enrollment in place of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque Waqf Estate. 

 21. It appears that when the Waqf Administrator gave enrollment in the name of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque Waqf Estate 36½ decimals land including 12 decimals of land in plot No 12163 was enlisted in the name of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque. The appellant's claim is that there is no existence of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque. It is their case that the Mosjid was established on the land in plot No. 12163 and the waqf estate is created by the deed dated 16-5-1940. 

 22. The respondent's case is that the mosque was established in the year 1895 by one Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir and after his death his successors managed the property. The land on which the Mosque was established recorded in the name of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosque. Whereas the appellant case is that Ashraf Ali Sharong established the mosque and subsequently he and others gifted 19 decimals land in the name of the mosque and the property was the waqf property of Kagadia Eshraful Ulum Madras Wafq Estate. Their further case is that the land was recorded in the name of Kagadia Eshraful Ulum Madrasha in RS khatian No. 209 and BS Khatian No. 2259. Whereas the respondent claims that the land was recorded in the name of successors of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir in BS Khatian No. 1199. 

 23. In view of the above facts, the dispute between the parties is not only with regard to the enrollment of waqf property but also a dispute of ownership of the property. Whether the land in dispute belonged to Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Masjid Waqf Estate or to Kagatia Eshatul Ulum Madrassa Waqf Estate needs to be resolved by evidence in a properly framed Civil Suit. 

 24. It further appears that the Waqf Administrator enrolled 24 decimal land which is said to have been leased out in favour of Hazrat Rupchand Shah (R) Fakir Mosjid Waqf Estate by the government and the land was enlisted as property of the Waqf Estate. 

 27. It also appears that by the subsequent order dated 30-9-2002 the Waqf Administrator virtually changed the name of the waqf estate and gave a supplementary enrollment in the name of Kagatia Eshatul Ulum Madrassa Waqf Estate in respect of 431/2 decimal land including 24 decimal leased out land and 1/2 decimal gifted land vide deed No. 4145 dated 30-11-1990 in place of Rupchan Shah (R) Fakir Mosjid Waqf Estate. 

 28. Section 47 of the waqf ordinance does authorize the Waqf Administrator to replace one waqf estate by another waqf estate and to give enrollment. In that view of the matter order dated 30-9-2002 is wrong and liable to be set-aside. Further Section 47 of the Waqf ordinance only authorizes the Waqf Administrator to give enrollment of Waqf property. The law under the section 47 does not authorize to appoint Mutually/Secretary. Therefore, the order of appointment of Md Tafazzal Hossain as secretary is also illegal. 

 29. The real dispute between the two waqf estates is a dispute of ownership of the land. The dispute requires judicial adjudication on evidence in a Civil Suit. The Additional district Judge failed to appreciate the real dispute between the parties and committed a wrong in setting aside the order dated 30-9-2002 only.
